Paycheck Calculator

A paycheck calculator determines your exact net take-home pay per pay period after deducting federal income tax, Social Security (6.2%), Medicare (1.45%), state income taxes, and pre-tax retirement or health deductions. It reveals how much deposited cash lands in your bank account every payday.

Formula and Calculation Method

Net paycheck calculation flow:

Taxable Wages = Gross Pay - Pre-Tax Deductions (401k, Health Insurance, HSA)
FICA Taxes = Social Security (6.2% up to wage base) + Medicare (1.45%)
Net Pay = Gross Pay - Federal Withholding - State Withholding - FICA - Post-Tax Deductions

Verified 2026 Tax Rules (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32): Social Security wage cap is inflation-adjusted for 2026.

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Bi-Weekly Paycheck for $78,000 Annual Salary ($3,000 Gross Bi-Weekly)
Input Values:
  • Gross Salary: $78,000 / year ($3,000.00 bi-weekly across 26 pay periods)
  • Filing Status: Single (standard withholding)
  • Pre-Tax 401(k): 5% ($150.00 / paycheck)
  • Pre-Tax Health Insurance: $75.00 / paycheck

1. Gross Pay per period = $3,000.00

2. Pre-tax deductions = $150.00 (401k) + $75.00 (health) = $225.00

3. FICA taxable ($3,000 - $75 health) = $2,925.00

- Social Security (6.2%) = $181.35

- Medicare (1.45%) = $42.41

4. Federal Income Tax Withholding = $278.50

5. Estimated State Income Tax (avg 4%) = $111.00

6. Total Deductions = $225.00 + $181.35 + $42.41 + $278.50 + $111.00 = $838.26

7. Net Take-Home Pay = $3,000.00 - $838.26 = $2,161.74

Result: Net Take-Home Pay: $2,161.74 per bi-weekly paycheck ($4,683.77 / month)

How to Use the Paycheck Calculator

  1. Enter your gross annual salary or hourly wage with hours worked per week.
  2. Select your pay frequency (Weekly, Bi-Weekly, Semi-Monthly, Monthly).
  3. Select your tax filing status (Single, Married Filing Jointly).
  4. Add pre-tax deductions (401k contribution %, health insurance, HSA).
  5. Review your exact net deposit and deduction breakdown per paycheck.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • State and local income tax rates vary by state, county, and school district jurisdiction.
  • Additional voluntary payroll deductions (union dues, FSA, supplemental life insurance) vary by employer.

Frequently Asked Questions About Paycheck Calculator

What is the FICA tax deducted from my paycheck?

FICA stands for the Federal Insurance Contributions Act. It consists of a 6.2% Social Security tax (capped at the annual wage base) and a 1.45% Medicare tax (uncapped, with an additional 0.9% surtax on high earners), matched dollar-for-dollar by your employer.

How do pre-tax deductions increase my take-home efficiency?

Pre-tax deductions (such as traditional 401(k) contributions and health insurance premiums) reduce your gross taxable income before federal and state taxes are calculated, saving you 12% to 24%+ in taxes on every dollar contributed.

What is the difference between bi-weekly and semi-monthly pay periods?

Bi-weekly employees receive 26 paychecks per year (every two weeks, producing two "three-paycheck" months per year). Semi-monthly employees receive exactly 24 paychecks per year (typically on the 15th and last day of each month).

How do I adjust my paycheck withholding if I get a big refund or owe taxes?

You can adjust your federal tax withholding at any time by submitting a revised IRS Form W-4 to your employer payroll department, utilizing deductions, other income, or extra withholding lines.

How does this tool connect to the Income Tax Calculator?

Our Income Tax Calculator analyzes comprehensive annual tax liabilities and progressive brackets. This Paycheck Calculator translates those annual numbers into your practical per-paycheck deposit amount.
